newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore drifts lower at close, focus on Parkway.
newsitem.headline: Singapore drifts lower at close, focus on Parkway.

text.p: Singapore shares ended a shade lower on Friday with market attention focused on reports DBS Land will raise its stake in Parkway Holdings, brokers said.

"The market's attention was focused on Parkway because of reports DBS Land will be increasing its stake in the company," said one. Shares of Parkway shot up 5.97 percent on the day to close at S$7.10 a share. Volume reached 2.82 million shares.
DBS Land declined comment on reports it would raise its stake in Parkway to more than 20 percent from the current 19.2 percent. The Strait Times Industrial closed 1.69 points down at 2,065.48 points.
The activity in Parkway also boosted the price of DBS Land as its share price climbed 2.88 percent to S$5.00 a share with total volume for the day reaching 2.76 million shares.
Total market volume rose to 123.65 million shares against the previous day's 100.9 million. The market was equally divided between gainers and losers at 175 each.

A large cross-trade of 11.7 million warrants was seen in Electronic Resources. Some 3.6 million shares was traded in engineering group L&M, which gained four cents to S$1.59, buoyed by the victory of ruling party in Indonesia.
